summary: Coronary angiography + PCI for NSTEMI. Right radial 6F access, 90% mid-LAD culprit stenosis, pre-dilated then one 3.0x18 mm drug-eluting stent, post-dilated, TIMI 3. Transient hypotension (95 systolic) and chest pain during balloon inflation, resolved. Contrast ~140 mL, fluoro 12 min, minimal blood loss. Radial band hemostasis, good distal perfusion. To CCU on dual antiplatelet (aspirin + ticagrelor).

key_facts.stent: one 3.0 x 18 mm drug-eluting stent to mid LAD
key_facts.hemodynamic_event: transient hypotension (95 systolic) + chest pain during balloon inflation, resolved

must.no_incision_language: handoff/opnote/family must NOT say 'incision' or 'wound' — this is percutaneous; access is a radial puncture
must.family_tone: reassuring, explains it was done through a small tube in the wrist artery, patient must lie still / keep the wrist still for a while, going to a heart monitoring unit
must.family_says_cardiologist: the closing line should reference the cardiologist, not 'surgeon'
